title: MSI mode bench
intro: Reproduce the measurements behind the RigPolice article https://rigpolice.com/system/articles/enable-msi-mode/ . `msi-bench.ps1` records the interrupt mode of every PCI device, ISR and DPC time per driver from a kernel trace, and a stall probe that counts every gap of 2 us or more in a spinning thread on a chosen CPU. The Superposition load below is the GPU-bound load for it.
needs: Run one interrupt-mode state per series (stock, then after `msi-mode-utility.ps1`, with a reboot between).
run: `.\msi-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Load superposition -PresentMon <path to PresentMon-2.6.0-x64.exe> -Device dxgkrnl.sys,HDAudBus.sys,Wdf01000.sys`, then the same with `-Phase msi`. Without a load, `-Seconds` sets the window and `-Cpu 0,5` picks the probe CPUs (a load takes its window from the recipe, so `-Seconds` is refused with `-Load`). `-Device` takes the drivers whose interrupts you care about: a 5 s pre-trace finds the CPU that takes most of each driver's ISRs and the probe runs there too. A WDDM GPU logs its ISR as `dxgkrnl.sys`, not as the vendor driver, and `Wdf01000.sys` groups every KMDF device (USB host controller, GPIO). The result holds a histogram of the gaps per probe and `msi-bench-<phase>-stalls.csv` lists every gap of 1 ms or more. Results go next to the script, or to `-OutDir`.
touch: one temporary ETW session named "NT Kernel Logger" that it starts and stops itself (twice with `-Device`: the pre-trace and the main trace), for `-Load` PresentMon with its own ETW session named `rigpolice-bench`, and the stall-probe threads
game: For `-Load` start the bench before the load: it waits for the load's process and, when the recipe names a start line, for that line in the game log, then waits the load pause and captures frame times with PresentMon while the kernel trace and the probes run. Do not touch the PC until it prints the result.
record: `msi-bench.ps1` adds the interrupt mode of every PCI device, the stall probe per CPU (histogram, percentiles, total stalled time, the devices behind each CPU), the trace clock type, the CPU picked per `-Device` driver next to the CPU the main trace shows for it, and, with `-Load`, the load build, whether the installed video config matches the shipped one (mismatched key names only), the names of launch flags outside the recipe (names only, no values), the frame statistics and the count of frames PresentMon lost to a present event buffer overflow (`presentMon.overflowedPresents`; a run that lost any is rejected). The device table names each PCI device and its driver, because the interrupt mode per device is the measurement.
